Fatal: The server can't write its data directory, running as uid 65534 gid 65534:
  DATA_ROOT /pkg/data is not writable (ENOENT)
  NEST_STORAGE_ROOT /pkg/data/nests is not writable (ENOENT)
  DATABASE_PATH /pkg/data is not writable (ENOENT)
Give that user ownership, e.g. `chown -R 65534:65534 <dir>`. The container image runs as
1000:1000; a volume written by an older image that ran as root needs this once. On Kubernetes
set podSecurityContext.fsGroup. See CONFIGURATION.md → Docker. If this check is wrong for your
storage (it reads permission bits), SKIP_DATA_DIR_CHECK=1 skips it.
